The analysis is a whole-brain, group-level contrast of movie-viewing under different kinship (social) conditions; it assesses social processing of a moral/kinship scenario. Meets global sample and whole-brain criteria and local social-processing criteria.

The contrast directly manipulates perceived kinship (genetic vs. non-genetic sisters) — a kinship/affiliation paradigm — and is a whole-brain group map, satisfying global and local affiliation/attachment criteria.

The analysis does not specifically measure social communication constructs (e.g., facial/eye-gaze processing or communicative production/reception). Missing required local inclusion criteria SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The task/contrast does not probe self-related processing (e.g., self-judgment or viewing one’s own image). Missing required local inclusion criteria PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

The contrast examines processing of others in a moral/kinship context and highlights areas implicated in mentalizing/empathy; it is a whole-brain group-level map meeting perception-of-others criteria.

This whole-brain, group-level contrast tests the same social manipulation (perceived kinship) and therefore addresses social processing, despite greater occipital ISC in this contrast. Meets global and local social-processing criteria.

The contrast contrasts perceived kinship conditions (non-genetic > genetic); the analysis targets kinship/affiliation effects at the whole-brain level and therefore meets affiliation/attachment criteria.
The contrast does not specifically index social communication processes (e.g., face or gaze processing); missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The contrast does not probe self-related judgments or self-awareness; missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

The contrast concerns perception/processing of other agents in a moral/kinship context (movie characters) and highlights regions relevant to mentalizing; meets global and perception-of-others criteria.
The GLM of the moral-dilemma decision task is a whole-brain group analysis of socially relevant moral decisions and therefore satisfies global and local social-processing criteria.

Although the moral decision task includes kin-related trials, the reported contrast (decision vs. non-decision) does not specifically compare loved-one vs. stranger conditions; missing the specific local inclusion criterion AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2 (contrast measuring affiliation/attachment, e.g., loved one vs stranger).

The GLM contrasts decision vs. non-decision and is not targeted to social communication constructs (faces/gaze/communication production or reception). Missing SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.

The moral decision GLM involves choosing between others (sister, friend, strangers) and localizes regions implicated in mentalizing/empathy, satisfying global criteria and perception-of-others inclusion criteria.

Group-level contrasts of an empathy/social-emotion task (SELF vs baseline) in healthy adults meet global criteria and the contrast measures social processing (emotional perspective taking).

Task contrasts do not probe affiliation/attachment constructs (e.g., kinship, cooperation, loved-one vs stranger). Missing required local inclusion criteria AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

SELF task uses viewing emotional faces and evaluating affective states; this maps onto social communication (reception of facial communication) and is a group-level whole-brain contrast in healthy adults.
SELF versus baseline explicitly measures perception/understanding of one's own emotional response (self-judgment), in a healthy adult group-level whole-brain contrast.
SELF-task contrast measures own emotional response rather than perception/understanding of others; missing PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Group-level OTHER vs baseline contrast in healthy adults measures empathic/social processing (evaluating others' emotional states) and meets global criteria.

OTHER-task measures perception of others, not self-judgment. Missing PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
OTHER versus baseline directly measures perception/understanding of others' emotional states (ToM/empathy), in a healthy adult group-level whole-brain contrast.

Global criteria met (healthy adult, whole-brain group voxelwise task map). Contrast compares self vs friend across face/name in a social recognition task, which measures social processing.

Contrast is self vs friend (self-specific), not a measure of affiliation/attachment (e.g., Loved one vs Stranger). Missing local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

Contrast pools face and name (self vs friend) and does not specifically test reception/production of facial or other social communicative signals (e.g., Faces > non-faces). Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Global criteria met. The contrast explicitly tests self > friend (self-specific activation across modalities), matching Perception/Self (Self > Other).
Contrast tests self > friend (self-specific), not a contrast measuring perception/understanding of others. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Face simple effect (Sf–Ff) is a social recognition task (face-based) in healthy adults using whole-brain group maps; meets social processing criteria.

Contrast compares self vs friend (self-specific face effect), not affiliation/attachment (Loved one vs Stranger). Missing local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This is a face-specific contrast (Sf–Ff); viewing faces and distinguishing identity is a form of reception of facial communication, meeting SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2.
Contrast tests Self (face) > Friend (face), matching Perception/Self criteria (self-judgment/viewing pictures of self).
Contrast is self > friend (face), not a measure of perception/understanding of others. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Name simple effect (Sn–Fn) examines social person-recognition using names in healthy adults with whole-brain group maps; fits social processing.

Contrast compares self-name vs friend-name (self-specific), not affiliation/attachment (Loved one vs Stranger). Missing local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

This contrast is name-based (Sn–Fn) and does not test reception/production of facial communication or equivalent social communicative signals as defined by the annotation. Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast tests Self (name) > Friend (name), a direct self > other comparison matching Perception/Self criteria.
Contrast is self-name > friend-name (self-specific), not directly measuring perception/understanding of others. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Face-specific interaction [(Sf–Ff)–(Sn–Fn)] isolates self-face processing, a social recognition task; global criteria met.

This is a self-face specific contrast (interaction), not an affiliation/attachment contrast (Loved one vs Stranger). Missing local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This is a face-specific interaction contrast isolating face-based self-recognition; viewing faces and extracting identity-related information meets SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2.
Contrast isolates self-face specificity (Self > Friend for faces relative to names), meeting Perception/Self criteria.
Contrast focuses on self-face specificity rather than perception/understanding of others. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Name-specific interaction isolates self-name processing; this is a social person-recognition task using whole-brain group maps.
This is a self-name specific contrast, not an affiliation/attachment contrast (Loved one vs Stranger). Missing local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

This contrast isolates name-based self-specific processing and does not target reception/production of facial or other canonical social communicative signals as defined. Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast isolates self-name specificity (Self > Friend for names relative to faces), matching Perception/Self criteria (self-judgment/viewing self stimuli).
Contrast focuses on self-name specificity rather than perception/understanding of others. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Friend > Self main effect across modalities probes social person-recognition and social processing (comparison among social categories) in healthy adults using whole-brain group analyses.

Contrast compares friend vs self (friend-specific), not the canonical affiliation contrast (Loved one vs Stranger or familiar vs unfamiliar). Missing local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.

This is a cross-modal friend > self contrast and not specifically a face-based social-communication contrast (e.g., Faces > non-faces). Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.

Contrast is friend > self (reverse of Self > Other), so it does not measure perception/self-related processes in the required direction. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Global criteria met. The contrast tests Friend > Self (others > self), which measures perception/understanding of others (friend-specific activation), matching PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and I2.
Face simple effect Ff–Sf examines friend (other) face recognition, a social processing task, using whole-brain group maps.
Contrast compares friend face vs self face, not a loved-one vs stranger contrast (affiliation). Missing local inclusion criteria: AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2.
This is a face-based contrast (friend face > self face); viewing faces and extracting identity/social cues fits SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2.
Contrast is friend > self (other > self) and thus does not test self-perception (Self > Other). Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Face contrast tests perception of another person (friend > self), meeting PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2 (perception/understanding of others).
Main effect (Sf+Ff+Sn+Fn–2(Cf+Cn)) contrasts familiar (self+friend) vs unfamiliar and probes social/person familiarity processing in a whole-brain task; fits social processing.
This contrast compares familiar (self+friend) vs unfamiliar (control), directly indexing affiliation/attachment-like familiarity (Loved one/familiar vs Stranger/unfamiliar).

This main familiarity contrast pools face and name and is not specifically a social-communication (face > non-face) contrast. Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast is familiarity (self+friend) vs unfamiliar and does not isolate Self > Other. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Contrast includes friend vs unfamiliar comparisons (familiar other vs unfamiliar), indexing perception/understanding of others and familiarity effects; meets PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Face familiarity simple effect (Sf+Ff–2Cf) examines familiar vs unfamiliar faces and is a social/person-recognition task meeting social processing criteria.
This face-specific familiar vs unfamiliar contrast directly indexes affiliation/attachment-like familiarity (familiar faces vs unfamiliar faces).
This is a face-based contrast (faces familiar > unfamiliar), matching SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 (reception of facial communication) and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
Contrast pools self and friend (familiar) > unfamiliar and does not isolate Self > Other. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Face familiarity contrast includes friend (other) > unfamiliar comparisons, indexing perception/understanding of others; meets PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
Name familiarity simple effect (Sn+Fn–2Cn) probes familiar vs unfamiliar name recognition, a social/person-recognition task using whole-brain maps.
This name-specific familiar vs unfamiliar contrast indexes affiliation/familiarity (familiar names vs unfamiliar) analogous to loved-one vs stranger contrasts.

This contrast is name-based (non-facial) and does not specifically target reception/production of facial communication as framed in SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1. Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.

Contrast pools self and friend (familiar) > unfamiliar and does not isolate Self > Other, so it does not meet Perception/Self criteria. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Name familiarity contrast includes friend (other) vs unfamiliar comparisons and thus indexes perception/understanding of others (familiar other representation).
Face-specific interaction of familiarity vs name [(Sf+Ff–2Cf)–(Sn+Fn–2Cn)] isolates face-based familiarity effects, a social processing contrast using whole-brain group maps.
This contrast isolates face-based familiar vs unfamiliar effects (face-specific familiarity), which indexes affiliation/attachment-like familiarity (familiar face vs unfamiliar face).
This is a face-specific interaction (face familiarity > name familiarity), directly probing reception of facial social communication; meets SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and I2.

This contrast isolates face vs name familiarity effects (familiarity modulation) and does not directly isolate Self > Other. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.

Face-specific familiarity interaction includes friend (other) vs unfamiliar comparisons in the face domain and thus measures aspects of perception/understanding of others (familiar other representation).
Name-specific interaction isolates name-based familiarity effects, a social/person-recognition contrast using whole-brain group analyses.
This contrast isolates name-based familiar vs unfamiliar effects and thus indexes affiliation/familiarity (familiar names vs unfamiliar), meeting the affiliation criteria.

This is a name-specific interaction (name familiarity > face familiarity) and does not specifically target reception/production of facial social communication as framed in SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1. Missing local inclusion criteria: SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
This contrast isolates name-based familiarity modulation and does not directly isolate Self > Other. Missing local inclusion criteria: PERCEPTION_SELF_I1 and PERCEPTION_SELF_I2.
Name-specific familiarity interaction includes friend (other) vs unfamiliar comparisons in the name domain and thus indexes perception/understanding of others (familiar other representation).

Healthy adult, whole-brain contrast comparing aggressive > disgusting faces; this examines social processing related to trait knowledge retrieval from faces.
Contrast is not assessing affiliation or attachment processes (missing AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I1 and AFFILIATION_ATTACHMENT_I2).

The contrast self-relevant > control is a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map in healthy adults examining recall of relationship episodes (a social task). It measures social processing (self- and other-referencing in relationships).

The task probes formative relationship episodes (close-relationship, attachment-relevant content) and the contrast compares self-relevant relationship recall to control, meeting affiliation/attachment task criteria.

Although social, this contrast does not target Social Communication constructs (e.g., face viewing, emotion recognition, gaze or direct communicative exchanges). Missing required local inclusion criteria SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I1 and SOCIAL_COMMUNICATION_I2.
The contrast directly probes self-referential recall (thinking about one's own formative relationship episodes) in a whole-brain group map, matching perception/understanding of self criteria.

This specific contrast (self-relevant > control) does not measure perception/understanding of others or theory-of-mind/empathy constructs. Missing required local inclusion criteria PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I1 and PERCEPTION_OTHERS_I2.
